Provisional License. On selection by the Commission, an applicant shall submit the
required license fee and subsequently be issued a provisional license to develop a Marijuana
Establishment, in the name of the entity. Such provisional license shall be subject to
reasonable conditions specified by the Commission, if any.

Provisional License. On selection by the Commission, an applicant shall submit the
required license fee and subsequently be issued a provisional license to develop a Marijuana
Establishment, in the name of the entity. Such provisional license shall be subject to
reasonable conditions specified by the Commission, if any.

The Commission shall review architectural plans for the building or renovation of a
Marijuana Establishment. Construction or renovation related to such plans may not begin
until the Commission has granted approval. Submission of such plans shall occur in a
manner and form established by the Commission including, but not limited to, a detailed
floor plan of the Premises of the proposed Marijuana Establishment that identifies the square

footage available and describes the functional areas of the Marijuana Establishment,
including areas for any preparation of Marijuana Products, and, if applicable, such
information for the single allowable off-Premises location in Massachusetts where Marijuana
will be cultivated or Marijuana Products will be prepared; and a description of plans to
ensure that the Marijuana Establishment will be compliant with requirements of the
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accessibility Guidelines.

To demonstrate compliance with {{ref:500.120(11)}}, a Marijuana Cultivator
applicant shall also submit an energy compliance letter prepared by a Massachusetts Licensed
Professional Engineer or Massachusetts Licensed Registered Architect with supporting
documentation. For a Microbusiness or Craft Marijuana Cooperative with a cultivation
location sized as Tier 1 or Tier 2, compliance with any of the requirements of {{ref:500.120(11)}} may be demonstrated through an energy compliance letter prepared by one or
more of the following energy professionals:
1. A Certified Energy Auditor certified by the Association of Energy Engineers;
2. A Certified Energy Manager certified by the Association of Energy Engineers;
3. A Massachusetts Licensed Professional Engineer; or
4. A Massachusetts Licensed Registered Architect.

A Marijuana Establishment shall construct its facilities in accordance with {{ref:500.000}}, conditions set forth by the Commission in its provisional license and architectural
review, and any applicable state and local laws, regulations, permits or licenses.

The Commission may conduct inspections of the facilities, as well as review all written
materials required in accordance with {{ref:500.000}}.

The applicable license fee shall be paid within 90 days from the date the applicant was
approved for a provisional license by the Commission. Failure to pay the applicable license
fee within the required time frame shall result in the license approval expiring. If this occurs,
a new license application will need to be completed pursuant to 935 CMR 500. 101 and will
require Commission approval.

To the extent updates are required to the information provided for initial licensure, the
Marijuana Cultivator shall submit an updated energy compliance letter prepared by a
Massachusetts Licensed Professional Engineer or Massachusetts Licensed Registered
Architect with supporting documentation, together with a renewal application submitted
under {{ref:500.103(4)}}.

Prior to the issuance of a final license, an Independent Testing Laboratory shall
demonstrate compliance with {{ref:500.050(7)(a)}} and provide to the Commission
documentation relating to its accreditation.

To the extent that an Applicant for a Delivery Operator License decides, following the
submission of the Application for Provisional Licensure, but prior to receiving Final
Licensure, that the Applicant will engage in White Labeling, the Applicant shall submit the
information required by {{ref:500.101(3)(h)}}4. to the Commission. The Executive
Director shall determine whether the submission satisfies the requirements of {{ref:500.101(3)(h)}}4.

To demonstrate compliance with {{ref:500.141(10)}}, a Social Consumption
Establishment applicant that intends to include an Indoor Smoking Consumption Area shall
also submit a ventilation and filtration compliance letter, bearing the stamp and signature of
a Massachusetts Licensed Mechanical Engineer in accordance with {{extref:M.G.L. c. 112, § 81}}M,
together with supporting documentation, including but not limited to plans, computations,
and specifications demonstrating system design and performance.

Final License. On completion of all inspections required by the Commission, a Marijuana
Establishment is eligible for a final license. All information described in {{ref:500.000}}
that is not available at the time of submission shall be provided to and approved by the
Commission before Marijuana Establishment may receive a final license. Such final licenses
shall be subject to reasonable conditions specified by the Commission, if any.

Final License. On completion of all inspections required by the Commission, a Marijuana
Establishment is eligible for a final license. All information described in {{ref:500.000}}
that is not available at the time of submission shall be provided to and approved by the
Commission before Marijuana Establishment may receive a final license. Such final licenses
shall be subject to reasonable conditions specified by the Commission, if any.

No person or entity shall operate a Marijuana Establishment without a final license
issued by the Commission.

A provisional or final license may not be assigned or transferred without prior
Commission approval.

A provisional or final license shall be immediately void if the Marijuana Establishment
Ceases to Operate or if, without the permission of the Commission, it relocates.

Acceptance of a provisional or final license constitutes an agreement by the Marijuana
Establishment that it will adhere to the practices, policies, and procedures that are described
in its application materials, as well as all relevant laws, regulations, and any conditions
imposed by the Commission as part of licensure.

The Marijuana Establishment shall post the final license in a conspicuous location on
the Premises at each Commission-approved location.
The Marijuana Establishment shall conduct all activities authorized by {{ref:500.000}} at the address(es) identified on the final license issued by the Commission.

Unless authorized by the Commission, a Marijuana Establishment may not sell any
service or good other than Marijuana and Marijuana Products, including MIPs and Marijuana
Seeds, Branded Goods, and Marijuana Accessories; provided however, that a Social
Consumption Establishment may sell other items in accordance with {{ref:500.141(3)(d)}}6.

The Marijuana Establishment shall be operational within the time indicated in {{ref:500.101(1)(c)}}5. or as otherwise amended through the application process and approved by the
Commission through the issuance of a final license.

Expiration and Renewal of Licensure. The Marijuana Establishment's license, as applicable,
shall expire one year after the date of issuance of the provisional license and annually thereafter,
and may be renewed as follows, unless an action has been taken based on the grounds set forth
in {{ref:500.450}}.

Expiration and Renewal of Licensure. The Marijuana Establishment's license, as applicable,
shall expire one year after the date of issuance of the provisional license and annually thereafter,
and may be renewed as follows, unless an action has been taken based on the grounds set forth
in {{ref:500.450}}.

No later than 90 calendar days prior to the expiration date, a Marijuana Establishment
shall submit a completed renewal application to the Commission in a form and manner
determined by the Commission, as well as the required license fee.

The Marijuana Establishment shall submit as a component of the renewal application
a report or other information demonstrating the establishment's efforts to comply with the
plans required under {{ref:500.101(1)}}, including {{ref:500.101(1)(a)}}11. and
{{ref:500.100(1)(c)}}8.k., as applicable. The report shall, at a minimum, have detailed,
demonstrative, and quantifiable proof of the establishment's efforts, progress, and success
of said plans.

A Marijuana Cultivator engaged in indoor cultivation shall include a report of the
Marijuana Cultivator's energy and water usage over the 12-month period preceding the date
of the application.

To the extent updates are required to the information provided for initial licensure, the
Marijuana Cultivator shall submit an updated energy compliance letter prepared by a
Massachusetts Licensed Professional Engineer or Massachusetts Licensed Registered
Architect with supporting documentation, together with a renewal application submitted
under {{ref:500.103(4)}}.

The Marijuana Establishment shall submit as a component of the renewal application
certification of good standing from the Secretary of the Commonwealth, the DOR, and the
DUA. Certificates of good standing will be valid if issued within 90 days of the submittal
of the renewal application.

The Marijuana Establishments shall update as needed, and ensure the accuracy of, all
information that it submitted on its initial application for a license.
The Marijuana Establishment shall comply with the requirements of {{ref:500.104(1)}} in accordance with that section separately from the renewal application.

Commission shall issue a renewal license within 30 days of receipt of a renewal
application and renewal license fee to a Licensee in accordance with {{extref:M.G.L. c. 94G, § 6}}, if
the Licensee:
1. Is in good standing with the Secretary of Commonwealth, DOR, and DUA;
2. Provided documentation demonstrating substantial effort or progress towards
achieving its goals submitted as part of its plans required under {{ref:500.101(1)}},
including {{ref:500.101(1)(a)}}11. and {{ref:500.101(1)(c)}}8.k., as applicable; and
3. No new information submitted as part of the renewal application, or otherwise
obtained, presents suitability issues for any individual or entity listed on the application
or license.

All Economic Empowerment Priority Applicants shall submit, as part of its renewal
application, an attestation in a form and manner determined by the Commission, executed
by the individuals who, through ownership, qualify an applicant or licensee as an Economic
Empowerment Priority Applicant certifying that:

All Economic Empowerment Priority Applicants shall submit, as part of its renewal
application, an attestation in a form and manner determined by the Commission, executed
by the individuals who, through ownership, qualify an applicant or licensee as an Economic
Empowerment Priority Applicant certifying that:

Is in good standing with the Secretary of Commonwealth, DOR, and DUA;
2. Provided documentation demonstrating substantial effort or progress towards
achieving its goals submitted as part of its plans required under {{ref:500.101(1)}},
including {{ref:500.101(1)(a)}}11. and {{ref:500.101(1)(c)}}8.k., as applicable; and
3. No new information submitted as part of the renewal application, or otherwise
obtained, presents suitability issues for any individual or entity listed on the application
or license.

CMO Marijuana Retailers shall submit the following information pertaining to patient
supply of Marijuana:
1. The licensee's policy and the procedures (e.g., data points, formulas) relied on to
determine what constitutes a sufficient quantity and variety of Marijuana Products
consistent with {{ref:500.140(15)}}; and
2. The licensee's policy and procedures for determining what qualifies as a reasonable
substitution for a medical Marijuana Product under {{ref:500.140(15)}} and its policy
for communicating reliance on the substitution to patients.

To the extent updates are required to the information provided for initial licensure, a
Social Consumption Establishment with an Indoor Smoking Consumption Area shall submit
an updated ventilation and filtration compliance letter, bearing the stamp and signature of a
Massachusetts Licensed Mechanical Engineer in accordance with {{extref:M.G.L. c. 112, § 81}}M,
together with supporting documentation, including but not limited to plans, computations,
and specifications, and a renewal application submitted under {{ref:500.103(4)}}.

The Commission shall maintain a publicly available and searchable source of information
about all operating licensees, including Delivery Licensees, on its website.
